items.prompt: Evaluate \(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{4}\). Give your answer as a fraction in lowest terms.
Solve \(2(x-1)+4=8\). Show your intermediate equations.

mark_scheme.text: Expand or rearrange the bracket term.
Isolate x using correct inverse operations.

items.prompt: A school has 180 pupils. \(10\%\) travel by bus. Calculate how many travel by bus.

mark_scheme.text: Convert the percentage into a fractional multiplier.

items.prompt: A bag contains 3 red and 5 blue tokens. One token is selected at random. Find the probability that it is red, as a simplified fraction.
Solve \[\begin{aligned}2x+y&=5\\x-y&=1\end{aligned}\] Show elimination or substitution.
Factorise and solve \(x^2-6x+5=0\). State both real roots.

mark_scheme.text: Choose two values with the correct sum and product.

items.prompt: A right-angled triangle has perpendicular sides \(3\text{ cm}\) and \(4\text{ cm}\). Calculate the hypotenuse exactly, showing your working.
A delivery van travels at \(40\text{ km/h}\) for \(45\text{ minutes}\). Calculate the distance it covers in kilometres, showing the unit conversion.

The measured length and width of a rectangle are \(4.2\text{ m}\) and \(2.7\text{ m}\), each rounded to the nearest \(0.1\text{ m}\). Find the exact upper bound for its area and explain your choice of bounds.

mark_scheme.text: Explain that the actual dimensions could exceed the recorded dimensions.

items.prompt: Write \(x^2-4x+(1)\) in completed-square form. Find the minimum value and the value of \(x\) at which it occurs.

mark_scheme.text: Complete the square and correct the constant.
Recognise that the squared term is non-negative.

items.prompt: In triangle \(ABC\), \(AB=3\text{ cm}\), \(AC=8\text{ cm}\) and \(\angle BAC=60^\circ\). Use the cosine rule to find \(BC\) exactly. Explain why it is appropriate.

mark_scheme.text: Recognise two sides and their included angle.
The sine rule has no known opposite side–angle pair.
